newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down across the board on Tuesday on an expected technical correction after the sharo gains of the past few days, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 11.8 percent from 16.0 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell sharply to 6.8 million losts from 14.2 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said Tuesday's fall had been predicted as the rates had risen too far too fast in the past few trading days.
The weak performance of the domestic A shares today was another factor behind the decline of the repo rates, traders said.
"Today's correction was expected," said a trader. "The repo rates are likely to go down further tomorrow."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Tuesday mainly due to the high yields of many contracts, traders said.
The most actively traded two-year note that matures in January 1999 rose to 85.40 yuan from 85.20 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose to 883,272 lots from 647,041 lots.
Besides the high yields of many contracts, rising risk on the domestic A share markets due to the recent strong gains also made some investors turn their backs on the spot market, traders said.
Traders said they believed the contracts would go up in the short-term.
